title: WPSS/2104/2023 of VIKAS KUKRETI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings
or directions and
Registrar's order with
Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.2104 of 2023
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
1. Mr. Siddhartha Bankoti, learned
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
3. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel
for respondent no.2.
4. Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
5. By means of this writ petition the
petitioner has sought the indulgence of
this Court directing the respondents to
grant age relaxation.
6. Brief facts of the case are that an
advertisement was issued by respondent
no.2 on 13.10.2023 inviting online
applications for graduate level Group-C
post for various departments in the State
of Uttarakhand and the last date of filing
of the online application is 23.11.2023.
On 06.11.2020, an advertisement was
issued by the respondent no.2-
Commission inviting applications for
graduate level Group-C post for various
departments of State of Uttarakhand;

petitioner submitted his candidature
pursuant to the aforesaid advertisement
dated 06.11.2020; this process was
culminated by recommending the
appointment and the appointment was
given to the successful candidates of
that selection process; the result was
declared on 21.07.2023.
7. It is submitted by the counsel for
the counsel for the petitioner that
though the petitioner submitted for his
candidature pursuant to the
advertisement dated 06.11.2020 but he
did not appear in said examination and
when the examination was cancelled and
it has been decided by the Commission
to hold re-examination, a caveat was
there that those candidates, who
participated in the examination, would
be entitled to re-appear in the re-examination.
8. But since the petitioner had not
avail the opportunity of writing the
examination held on first occasion, he
was not permitted to participate in the
re-examination so held by respondent
no.2.

9. The petitioner contends that since
there is lapse on the part of the
respondents/State by not permitting him
in the re-examination, due to which he
has become over age by nine months,
he should be granted age relaxation by
the respondents to file his online
application pursuant to the fresh
advertisement dated 13.10.2023.
10. This submission of the learned
counsel for the petitioner does not
appear to be convincing for the reason
being that it is not the lapse of
Government or the respondents
authorities rather it is the lapse on the
part of the petitioner to fail to write
examination pursuant to earlier
advertisement dated 06.11.2020
consequent to which he was not allowed
to participate in the re-examination.
11. The petitioner have had an
opportunity to challenge that decision of
respondent no.2/Commission for not
allowing him to appear in re-examination
but the petitioner remained slept over
his rights and now he has filed the
present writ petition.

12. This Court is not impressed by the
submission made by the petitioner.
Selection pursuant to earlier
advertisement dated 06.11.2020 having
been concluded in which the petitioner
did not appear, this cannot come to
rescue of the petitioner.
13. In this view of the matter, the writ
petition is devoid of merits and the same
is accordingly dismissed.
